title: The reporter
request: Let a model write the report's prose for the people who own a decision, but keep a sentence only when it is grounded in the records, and keep the deterministic report when nothing passes.
spec: The report's prose (17.7) written by a model from the records and kept sentence by sentence only when cited.py passes it; the deterministic report when nothing passes. Done when the replicas' reports are written with the model on and off, and no kept sentence fails the check.
plan: Keep every line code wrote; let the model add a short summary above each prose section, citing the section's own lines.
Keep a sentence only through the host's check (cited.py), and never keep model text without one: dclab_core takes the check as an argument.
Give the role a purpose and a data-limit test; add the advisor path to the studio's report, never for a private project.
Fix a gate before any run and build a harness that re-checks every kept sentence independently.
Review before the paid run, fix, then measure once live under the owner's cap.

decisions.decision: The model adds a summary above the lines rather than rewriting them.
decisions.why: A rewrite could drop a fact; an addition cannot, and nothing passing leaves the report exactly as code wrote it.

decisions.decision: dclab_core keeps nothing a model writes unless the host passes a check.
decisions.why: The core must stay pure (cited.py lives in dclab_rnd) and a host that forgets the check must not get unchecked prose.

decisions.decision: Wait for the review before the owner-approved live run.
decisions.why: Earlier measurements taught that a harness bug found after a paid or sealed run cannot be fixed without repeating it.

change: REPORTER role, write_prose and the strict sentence rules in dclab_core/report.py; prompt reporter.md; purpose reporter with its data limits; solution_report.build(advisor=...); the roles harness's measure_reporter, reporter_verdict and reporter_gate_v1; tests for the role, the harness, rendering, the private path and the data limits.

findings.defect: A denial that cited.py accepts broke the report's strict readiness rule.
findings.scenario: 'The model is not yet production-ready and should not go live before a review [L1]' was kept, and the report's own check then said a sentence calls a model production-ready.
findings.cause: cited.py excuses a denial; the report's rule (17.7) is strict.
findings.fix: A kept sentence must also pass the report's own overclaim rule; the harness re-check uses it too.

findings.defect: Number forms cited.py accepts did not trace under the report's rules.
findings.scenario: 'Positives are 18.4 percent of the training rows [L3]' was kept; the report's check then said 18.4 is not traced to a record.
findings.cause: cited.py reads 'percent' as '%'; the report's tracer does not.
findings.fix: Every number must be written exactly as the cited line writes it; the harness runs the report's own check on the written report.

findings.defect: Model text went into the report unescaped.
findings.scenario: A summary with an HTML tag was kept raw in the Markdown, and one with mis-nested backticks and bold made the PDF renderer raise, losing the whole PDF.
findings.cause: Record text passes through render(); the summary did not.
findings.fix: Every kept sentence is rendered like record text.

findings.defect: True numbers beside the wrong subject passed every check.
findings.scenario: 'The final model reached an accuracy of 0.816' cited the baseline's line; 'used once, so its score is unbiased' cited a line that said used 3 times.
findings.cause: The checks only asked that a number appear somewhere in the cited lines.
findings.fix: Each number must stand beside two of the words that stand before it in its line (metric and subject); quantity and quality words such as once or unbiased must appear in a cited line; the paragraph is labelled as a model's.

findings.defect: On multiclass projects the reporter saw the target's class names, against a stated limit of zero values.
findings.scenario: Per-class results and confused pairs in the report put class markers in the reporter's request; the data-limit test used a binary target only.
findings.cause: The limit was declared without a multiclass case.
findings.fix: The purpose declares the target's class names and range and allows them, and a multiclass test proves that no input column's value reaches the model.

findings.scenario: No test showed a private project sending nothing, the gate failing on a bad sentence, or a prose report rendering.
findings.cause: Only the passing echo path was tested.
findings.fix: Tests for the private path, an injected untraceable sentence failing the gate, and Markdown, HTML and PDF rendering.

findings.defect: dclab_core's list of roles left the reporter out.
findings.scenario: A host routing roles by roles() (the main product) would not see the reporter, and the prompt test skipped it.
findings.cause: The new role was not added to the list.

findings.defect: The first strict-rule version dropped every sentence.
findings.cause: cited.check returns kept sentences without their citations, which it lists separately, so no cited line was found.
findings.fix: Read the cited lines from the check's cites.

measurements.name: reporter on three replicas, live (ROL-006)
measurements.gate: reporter_gate_v1, fixed before the run: on the binary, multiclass and regression replicas, no kept sentence fails an independent re-check, every section's lines stay intact, and a sentence is kept in at least two of the three reports.
measurements.result: 28 sentences kept and 6 dropped across the 3 reports (binary 7 and 4, multiclass 9 and 2, regression 12 and 0); 0 failed the re-check; lines intact in all 3.
measurements.against_gate: 0 sentences failed the re-check, as required; lines stayed intact in all 3 reports; sentences were kept in all 3 reports, where 2 were required.
limits: One run with one model on three replicas; another model or another run could keep different sentences.
The checks prove the numbers and the claim words, not that a sentence's emphasis is fair: a person should read the summaries.
Replica reports, not a real project's.
measurements.next: Read the kept sentences with the owner before switching the reporter on in the product.

outcome: Done: model-written summaries above the report's lines, kept only through two layers of checks; measured once live and passed.
lessons: Two checks with different rules disagree at their edges: a kept sentence must pass the stricter one, and the harness must run both.
A number in the right source can still sit beside the wrong subject: check the words that stand before it.
Wait for the review before a paid run.
risks: A model rounds or converts a number and a lenient check keeps it.
A summary puts a true number beside the wrong subject.
Model text breaks a renderer or injects markup.
The reporter sees values of the user's data.
A private project's report reaches a model.
